critical_steps: The source distinguishes GB from GB+ and states both the factor and tensor controlled-frame definitions for controls in GB.
With U=U1=-I and T=T1=I, each factor energy is minus the squared norm.
The tensor controls multiply to identities, so the one-block tensor family is Parseval.
The source reverse proof divides a positive tensor inequality by a merely nonzero factor energy; sign control is missing.
Assuming nonnegative factor energies makes that division valid and gives explicit two-sided factor bounds.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact one-dimensional real counterexample plus a direct positivity-based repair of the factorization proof.
integrity.unproved_limits: No weakest repair for complex-valued controlled quadratic forms is characterized.

scientific_limitations: The finding refutes the reverse implication of Theorem 4 under its printed arbitrary-invertible-control convention.
Nonnegative factor controlled energies give a sufficient repair; no claim is made that positivity of the individual control operators alone is a necessary-and-sufficient condition.
The exact sign dichotomy is stated only for real-valued controlled energies; no full complex-phase classification is asserted.
title: A sign obstruction to the tensor-product characterization of controlled \(g\)-fusion frames
